# `sandloom.sdk.authz`

Authorization: policies and atoms, access facts, the billing-account subject
(`Account`).

Public API 1.0 (spec §2.2, Appendix C).

`from sandloom.sdk.authz import <name>`. Signatures in a terminal: `sandloom docs <name>`. Beginner names are the ones generated code and the examples use; any other name is advanced (mark its import line `# sandloom: advanced <reason>` in generated code and examples).

## Beginner names

### `authorize_resource`

```python
def authorize_resource(
    *,
    loader: Callable[[Any, AsyncSession], Awaitable[Any]],
    by: str,
    policy: Requirement,
    cast: Callable[[str], Any] | None = None,
    not_found_detail: str = 'Not found',
    status_code: int | None = None,
) -> Callable[..., Awaitable[Any]]
```

Load a resource by path id, authorize, and return it to the endpoint.

**Args:**

- `loader`: `async (id_value, db) -> entity | None` — the module supplies its own loader (keeps `shared` free of ORM imports).
- `by`: name of the path parameter holding the resource id.
- `policy`: requirement to enforce; resource atoms (`Owner`) read the loaded entity.
- `cast`: optional converter applied to the raw path value before `loader` (e.g. `UUID`). Defaults to passing the raw string.
- `not_found_detail`: 404 message when the loader returns `None`.
- `status_code`: explicit status override for a definite denial (default: the decision's own status).

The resource is fetched **once**: claim atoms evaluate first, so a failing
cheap check raises without ever loading; otherwise the entity loaded for
the ownership check is the same one returned to the endpoint.

### `OrgRole`

```python
class OrgRole(Requirement)(
    minimum: str,
    *,
    org_param: str = 'org_id',
    adapter: Any = None,
) -> None
```

Subject holds at least `minimum` role in the request's organization.

Relationship (ReBAC) authorization: org membership/role is per-organization
and not carried in the global JWT, so it is resolved live through the
membership contract (local call in a monolith, an RPC when tenancy is a
separate service; 501 when neither). The organization id is read from the
request path parameter `org_param`, else `X-Tenant-Id`, else the bound
tenant; a missing organization is indeterminate (denies even under `Not`).

For a hot path, a module may instead maintain an authorization projection of
memberships and gate on a projection-backed `Entitled` fact.

Non-empty for an atom that resolves an organisation (path parameter,

### `require`

```python
def require(
    policy: Requirement,
    *,
    status_code: int | None = None,
) -> Callable[..., Awaitable[UserContext]]
```

Return a dependency enforcing `policy` (no request resource).

Use in `dependencies=[Depends(require(...))]` or as a parameter when the
endpoint wants the resulting `UserContext`. A denial answers with the
decision's own status (e.g. `Subscribed(of=Account.user())` → 402, a
missing contract → 501);
`status_code` is an explicit override for definite denials.

A claims-only policy (every atom tier 1) never opens a database session /
Unit of Work; only policies that may reach a live atom depend on
`get_db`.

Raises `ValueError` at wiring time if `policy` contains a resource-scoped
atom (e.g. `Owner`): `require` has no request resource, so such a policy
belongs in `authorize_resource` / `authorize`.

### `Subscribed`

```python
class Subscribed(Requirement)(
    statuses: frozenset[str] | None = None,
    *,
    of: Account = <object object>,
    claim_key: str = 'subscription_status',
) -> None
```

Subject's subscription grants access (coarse, claim-based).

`of=Account.user()`: reads the token's
`subscription_status` claim with ZERO I/O, interpreted by the
`subscription.active` access fact — billing's declarative rule, the same
predicate as the live check (`active`/`trialing` pass; `past_due`
passes during the grace period unless `BILLING_DENY_ON_PAST_DUE`). The
fact is the local registration or, in a process without billing, the one
billing publishes over `billing.facts.v1` (described once, cached).

Provenance is honoured: when the token's authoritative provenance shows
billing did NOT contribute (it failed at mint, or the issuer could not
reach it) the claim proves nothing, so the atom escalates to billing's LIVE
answer instead of denying 402 for the token's whole lifetime (503
indeterminate when no live path exists). With no subscription owner in
the deployment at all, only `active`/`trialing` pass. May be up to the
token TTL stale; for real-time / money-sensitive checks use
`sandloom.shared.authz.atoms_live.SubscriptionActive` / `Credits`.

`of=Account.org(...)`: the token carries NO per-organization
subscription claim (claims are personal-only), so this atom resolves LIVE
— it delegates to `SubscriptionActive(of=...)` and is a tier-3 atom.
`of=Account.bound_tenant()` resolves the bound tenant's kind first
(personal → the claim, organization → live).

Passing explicit `statuses` pins the accepted set verbatim (no grace
interpretation).

### `AccessDecision`

```python
class AccessDecision(
    allowed: bool,
    code: str = 'ok',
    category: str | None = None,
    reason: str = '',
    http_status: int = 200,
    failed_requirement: str | None = None,
    policy_code: str | None = None,
    metadata: dict[str, Any] = <factory>,
    indeterminate: bool = False,
) -> None
```

The outcome of evaluating a policy against an `AuthzContext`.

`allowed` is the only field that matters for the boolean question; the
rest exist so a denial is reportable, auditable and observable.

#### `AccessDecision.error`

```python
@classmethod
def error(
    cls,
    *,
    code: str,
    category: str = 'policy_misconfigured',
    reason: str = '',
    http_status: int | None = None,
    failed_requirement: str | None = None,
    metadata: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> AccessDecision
```

An *indeterminate* denial: the requirement could not be evaluated.

Distinct from `deny` (the subject definitively lacks the
requirement): combinators propagate it unchanged, so `~Entitled(x)`
with `x` unregistered / its service down DENIES with this category and
status instead of inverting the failure into an allow.


Copy of this decision tagged with `policy_code`.

```python

```

The subset safe and useful to record on a deny (no PII).

### `AccessDenied`

```python
class AccessDenied(HTTPException)(
    decision: AccessDecision,
    *,
    status_code: int | None = None,
) -> None
```

Raised by `enforce` (and the HTTP guards) when a policy is not satisfied.

Carries the full `AccessDecision` so the caller (HTTP adapter, task
runner) can map it to the right transport response. Subclasses FastAPI's
`HTTPException` so a module calling `enforce()` inside an endpoint gets
the decision's status (402/403/501/…) and `{"detail", "code"}` body from
the framework HTTP handler instead of an unhandled 500. Non-HTTP callers
(workers, services) still catch the typed `AccessDenied` and read
`.decision`. It also exposes the framework error-protocol attributes
`http_status` / `code` / `detail`.

`status_code` explicitly overrides the decision's status (transport
override, e.g. `require(..., status_code=402)`).

### `AccessFact`

```python
class AccessFact(
    name: str,
    owner_module: str,
    claim_key: str | None = None,
    projection_reader: ProjectionReader | None = None,
    live_service: str | None = None,
    live_resolver: LiveResolver | None = None,

    deny_category: str | None = None,

```

Declarative binding of a fact name to its three resolution paths.

A module registers one of these in `register(core)` via
`core.register_access_fact(...)`, wiring together mechanisms that already
exist: its claims contributor (`claim_key`), an optional local projection
(`projection_reader`) and its service contract (`live_service` +
`live_resolver`).

### `authorize`

```python
async def authorize(
    resource: Any,
    policy: Requirement,
    *,
    ctx: UserContext,
    request: Request | None = None,
    db: AsyncSession | None = None,
    status_code: int | None = None,
) -> None
```

Inline check over an already-loaded `resource`; raises on failure.

The escape hatch for cases that don't fit `authorize_resource`
(multiple resources, ownership known only after a non-trivial query, authz
interleaved with business logic). The endpoint owns the single fetch.
Raises `AccessDenied` with the decision's status (or the explicit
`status_code` override for a definite denial).

#### `AuthzContext.get_resource`

Loading is lazy so that a policy like `Perm("x") & Owner(...)` never

#### `AuthzContext.has_resource`

```python
has_resource  (property)
```

#### `AuthzContext.core`

```python
def core(self) -> Any
```

Resolve the bound `CoreFacade`, or None.

Order: an explicitly-passed core (non-HTTP paths pass `core=` to
`enforce`) → the app the request was served by. There is deliberately
**no** process-global fallback — the subsystem never reaches a global
singleton (that would break multi-app / test isolation). When no core is
bound, atoms that need one (live / fact / `OrgRole`) degrade
explicitly (indeterminate 501 / `FactUnavailable`).

### `ClaimRule`

```python
class ClaimRule(kind: str = 'truthy', values: frozenset[Any] = frozenset()) -> None
```

Declarative claim -> bool interpretation: wire-safe, no callables.

`ClaimRule.one_of({"active", "trialing"})` is True iff the claim value is
one of the listed scalars; `ClaimRule.truthy()` is `bool(value)`. The
owner describes its facts with these, so a consumer in another process
interprets the token claim EXACTLY like the owner does locally (one source
of truth). A rule that depends on the owner's settings (billing's
`past_due` grace) is a zero-argument factory on the fact
(`AccessFact(claim_rule=factory)`), serialized with the owner's current
settings at `describe()` time.

### `enforce`

```python
async def enforce(
    policy: Requirement,
    *,
    subject: UserContext,
    db: AsyncSession | None = None,
    request: Request | None = None,
    resource: Any = <object object>,
    loader: Callable[[AuthzContext], Awaitable[Any]] | None = None,
    source: str = 'internal',
    core: Any = None,
    policy_code: str | None = None,
) -> AccessDecision
```

Evaluate `policy` for `subject`; raise `AccessDenied` on deny.

The one chokepoint. HTTP/use-case/task adapters all call this. Returns the
allow `AccessDecision` on success so callers may inspect it.

### `Entitled`

```python
class Entitled(Requirement)(
    fact_name: str,
    *,
    category: str | None = None,
    code: str | None = None,
    mode: str | None = None,
) -> None
```

Subject satisfies the registered access fact `fact_name`.

**Args:**

- `fact_name`: name of an `AccessFact` registered via `core.register_access_fact(...)`.
- `category`: denial category when the fact is False. Defaults to the fact's own `deny_category` (billing's subscription facts declare `Category.PAYMENT_REQUIRED` → 402), else `forbidden` (403). A resolver raising `FactDenied` picks its own category.
- `mode`: force a resolution mode, overriding the `ACCESS` setting (for tests / special endpoints). Normally left `None`.

A module's derived `consumes` includes them (optional), so the
startup preflight reports an unbound one and `sandloom add deploy`
binds it in a split deployment. Default: none (a claims-only atom).

### `FactDenied`

```python
class FactDenied(Exception)(
    reason: str,
    *,
    category: str = 'forbidden',
    code: str | None = None,
) -> None
```

A resolver's *definite* denial for a reason other than "the fact is False".

Raised by a projection reader / live resolver when the fact is
inapplicable to the subject — e.g. `organization.subscription.active`
with no organization in context, or for an org the subject is not a
member of. `sandloom.shared.authz.atoms_fact.Entitled` maps it to a
definite deny with `category` (default `forbidden`, 403) instead of
the fact's `deny_category` — "you may not ask" is not "pay to unlock".

### `FactOwnerUnreachable`

```python
class FactOwnerUnreachable(FactUnavailable)
```

The fact's owner is bound but could not describe its facts (503).

Distinct from "not configured" (501): the deployment is correct, the
owner is down. Never a silent allow or a definite deny.

### `FactUnavailable`

```python
class FactUnavailable(Exception)
```

A fact could not be resolved in any acceptable mode (a misconfiguration).

Raised when an explicitly-requested mode cannot be honored (live service not
bound, no projection reader) or `auto` exhausts every option. The atom
maps this to a `policy_misconfigured` decision — never a silent allow.

### `lookup_access_fact`

```python
async def lookup_access_fact(ctx: AuthzContext, name: str) -> AccessFact | None
```

The fact `name`: the local registration, else the owner's public one.

Order: `core.get_access_fact(name)` (owner co-deployed) → every bound
`<owner>.facts.v1` with no local provider (the owner named by the fact's
first dotted segment first), whose `describe()` is cached on the core for
`REMOTE_FACT_TTL_SECONDS`. `None` when no owner knows the fact (the
caller reports 501); `FactOwnerUnreachable` (503) when a bound owner
could not be asked and none of the others knows it.

### `make_rebuild_gate`

```python
def make_rebuild_gate(rebuilder: Any, *, name: str = '') -> StartupTask
```

A startup task that rebuilds an authz projection from its sources.

Captures the `rebuilder` supplied at registration in its closure (no
process-global / registry lookup at run time). Install as `critical=True`
so the process refuses traffic until the projection is populated — otherwise
an empty table makes every fact resolve False and the consumer
fail-closed-denies all callers. The rebuilder must be idempotent (the
protocol guarantees it), so re-running on boot is safe; for large
projections prefer `sandloom projection rebuild <name>` in the one-shot migrate
step with `rebuild_on_startup=False`.

### `Not`


### `Or`

```python
class Or(Requirement)(*parts: Requirement) -> None
```

Disjunction: any operand may hold. Short-circuits on first allow.

Only a genuinely satisfied operand allows — and one that does allows even
if a sibling is indeterminate (`Role("admin") | Entitled("x")` admits an
admin while the `x` fact is unregistered): the grant comes from the
satisfied operand, never from inverting or guessing the broken one. When
none allows and at least one operand was indeterminate, the disjunction is
indeterminate (the first such decision is returned, preserving its
category/status) — a broken branch is reported, not silently folded into a
plain 403.

### `PolicyIndeterminate`

```python
class PolicyIndeterminate(Exception)(decision: AccessDecision) -> None
```

Raised by an atom's `evaluate` when it cannot answer at all.

`evaluate` is boolean, so an atom that cannot evaluate (service absent,
fact unregistered, no tenant context) must not answer `False` — a caller
composing `not await atom.evaluate(ctx)` would turn the failure into an
allow. It raises this instead; `Requirement.decide` (and `enforce`)
convert it into the carried indeterminate `AccessDecision`. Never an
`HTTPException` — atoms run in workers too.

### `register_authz_projection`

```python
def register_authz_projection(
    core: Any,
    *,
    descriptor: Any,
    consumers: list[Any],
    rebuilder: Any,
    rebuild_on_startup: bool = False,
    critical: bool = True,
) -> None
```

Register an authorization projection, its consumers and rebuilder.

`descriptor` is a `QueryProjectionDescriptor`; `consumers` a list of
`ProjectionConsumerDescriptor` (one per source channel); `rebuilder` a
`ProjectionRebuilder`. When `rebuild_on_startup` is True a rebuild gate
is installed (`critical` controls whether its failure aborts startup).

### `register_live_adapter`

```python
def register_live_adapter(kind: str, adapter: Any) -> None
```

Bind the adapter the live atoms use for `kind` — CONSUMER-side config.

`kind` is `ENTITLEMENTS` or `MEMBERSHIP`; `adapter` must
satisfy `EntitlementsAdapter` / `MembershipAdapter`.

The table is per PROCESS and is read where the atom is EVALUATED — the
consumer. Register an adapter from the consumer's composition root or the
consuming module's `register(core)`, in every process that evaluates
`Credits` / `SubscriptionActive` / `OrgRole`. A provider module that
registers an adapter for its OWN contract only affects processes that
load it: in a split deployment the consumer process silently keeps the
default — so that is logged as a warning.

### `Requirement`

```python
class Requirement(ABC)
```

An authorization predicate, composable with `& | ~`.

`evaluate` is the primitive boolean check (it raises
`PolicyIndeterminate` when it cannot answer). `decide` wraps it
into a structured `AccessDecision` (the engine/enforcement path uses
`decide` so a denial carries a machine-readable code/category and the
failing requirement); the two never disagree.

### `WithinLimit`

```python
class WithinLimit(_AccountClaimAtom)(
    key: str,
    used: int,
    *,
    of: Account = <object object>,
    claim_key: str = 'limits',
) -> None
```

`used` is strictly below the account's plan limit for `key`.

For `Account.user()` the limit comes from the token claim; `used` is
the current count the caller already knows (e.g. number of seats). Absent
/ non-integer limit ⇒ treated as 0 (i.e. denied), so a missing entitlement
fails closed.
